chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufadhal ibn Umar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the meaning of the saying of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) when he looked at the Second (Umar) while he was covered with his garment: 'Nothing is more beloved to me than to meet Allah with a journal from this covered one.' He said: He meant by it the journal which was written in the Ka'ba.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Believers (Title of Imam Ali)
key_terms.الثَّانِي: The Second (Referring to Umar ibn al-Khattab)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali mean by 'the covered one' and 'the journal' in relation to Umar ibn al-Khattab?
ai.summary: This narration from *Mani al-Akhbar* highlights the Shia scholarly appreciation of Umar ibn al-Khattab, interpreting Imam Ali’s reference to him as 'the covered one' with affection rather than criticism. The 'journal' (sahifa) is identified as the record of his caliphate or deeds inscribed in the Ka'ba, suggesting a positive theological evaluation of his tenure despite historical differences. This reflects the nuanced Shia tradition of acknowledging the merits of the Rightly Guided Caliphs while maintaining distinct theological positions.

en.basel-kadem: 102.	We were told by Muhammed bin Ali Majilawayh, from his paternal uncle, Muhammed bin Abi’l-Qasem, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammed bin Sinan, from Mufadhal bin Umar, that he said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s.) about the meaning of the saying of the Commander of the Believers (AS) when he looked at the Second (Umar) while he was covered in his cloth: "Nothing is more beloved to me that I meet Allah with a journal from this covered person." He said: By that, he meant the journal which he wrote in the Ka’ba.
